is carried in full to the member, gaining where the market carries and losing where it is inverted."

restated in force. It is recorded here because a reader meets the same words on both sides of the
"no longer in force" line.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the prose of the twenty-eight documents in this task's scope was traced to a
structured source. Two claims have no source, and one source atom has no home.

### F2 — `KB-BIJECTION RED`: two clauses added to the balance computation document

**Document:** `docs/grain/striking_the_balance_still_owed_512f95c7.json`, section "How the credit is
assembled", third sentence.

**KB text:**

> "Handling shrink on conditioned loads, **where it arises at all**, is taken on the net bushels of
> every load standing against the contract, whatever the facility and whatever the disposition,
> **meaning the loads applied to the contract and the loads run straight through together**."

**Source text** (`grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation.rule`, and `compute_basis.handling_shrink_bu`):

> "Handling shrink on conditioned loads is taken on the net bushels of every load standing against
> the contract, whatever the facility and whatever the disposition."

Two additions:

1. **"where it arises at all"** — a hedge on a quantity the immediately preceding sentence has just
   declared nil ("No handling shrink is taken on conditioned loads"). The source's `baseline.rule`
   contains neither the hedge nor the basis sentence; the basis sentence belongs to the full policy
   `rule` and to the `conditioning_handling_shrink` factor's domain. Recorded again under
   `dependency_form` for what the hedge does to the reader.
2. **", meaning the loads applied to the contract and the loads run straight through together"** — a
   definitional equation the source states nowhere. It fixes "the loads applied to the contract" as a
   set that excludes the loads run straight through. Two factor ladders of two **other** policies
   are gated on "the net bushels applied to the contract"
   (`grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge.factors[volume_free_days]` and
   `grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge.factors[crop_year_roll_allowance]`), and their `compute` binds
   that phrase to every `grain_delivery_applied` row without a `disposition` filter. The added gloss
   therefore carries the reader to the opposite extension from the one the source computes, which is
   what makes the runtime failure recorded in `runtime_context/grain_marketing_desk/0.md` bite.

**Why this is a change of meaning, not a same-source restatement.** As a restatement of its own
sentence the gloss is true in this world; but a restatement may not introduce a term definition that
governs other policies' sentences. Here it does, and the definition it introduces contradicts the
source's own binding of the same words elsewhere.

### F1 (recorded here for completeness) — the phrase's two readings

The reverse scan confirms that the sentences carrying "the net bushels applied to the contract" in
`free_days_earned_by_what_is_hauled_5b04ebad.json` and
`bushels_rolled_free_in_a_crop_year_83eea126.json` are **verbatim faithful** to the source's ladder
text. The corpus is therefore not at fault for the words themselves; it is at fault for supplying, in
F2, the gloss that resolves them the wrong way, and the source is at fault for a ladder condition
whose words do not determine its own binding. The runtime consequence is recorded as
`KB-RUNTIME RED` in `runtime_context/grain_marketing_desk/0.md`; the policy-side half is recorded
under "Policy-side notes" below. No repair is proposed here.

### F4 — `KB-BIJECTION RED`: a source atom with no home (the crop-year window)

**Source:** `measures`:

> `grain_msr_crop_year_delivered_bushels` — `window: the current crop year, which runs 1 September
> through 31 August and is named for the calendar year in which it ends`
> `grain_msr_crop_year_rolls` — `window: the current crop year, which runs 1 September through 31
> August`

**KB:** no document in `docs/grain/` states when a crop year begins or ends (exact-string search for
"1 September" / "31 August" / "crop year runs" over all 73 documents returns nothing), although the
count it bounds is normative in two places that *are* carried:

- `rolling_rather_than_defaulting_689b5d0c.json` clause 2: "the contract may take no more rolls in a
  crop year than the programme allows";
- `roll_allowances_by_programme_dabb5093.json`: "The roll ceiling is a count for one crop year on one
  contract."

A reader asked whether a contract has reached its roll ceiling therefore has the ceiling but not the
window it is counted over. The same measure block also carries, for
`grain_msr_unpriced_carry_days`, the branch "or through the handling date where it is still open",
which no document carries; that branch is arguably superseded by the extended baseline's counting
sentence, so it is recorded as the lesser half of this finding.

**Effect on this task:** none. The contract's `roll_count` is 1 against a Hedge-to-Arrive ceiling of
4, and the free-roll allowance is a bushel figure, not a count. It is recorded because the whole
domain is audited, not only the branch the seed hits.

### Policy-side notes (reported, not counted toward this skill's verdict)

- **P1 — "struck in whole bushels" has no rounding mode.** The phrase governs the result of
  `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation` (and of three other computations in this difficulty), and
  neither the source's `rule`/`baseline.rule` nor the KB says whether it rounds or truncates; only
  the `compute` expression `RND(…, 0)` pins it. In this task the credited bushels come to 20,249.39,
  so the balance is 19,750.61 and the reader must choose between 19,750 and 19,751 — and the choice
  propagates into the roll charge. The documents are faithful to the source; the gap is the source's.
- **P2 — one rounding point or seven.** `money_released_on_a_settlement_statement` says the money is
  "rounded to the cent once at the end", verbatim from `baseline.rule`, while the source's `compute`
  rounds the freight, damage, foreign-material, retain and charge components to the cent individually
  before the final rounding. On this task's figures the two agree at 5,624.30, but they need not in
  general. Source-side.
- **P3 — the class ceiling at zero.** `capital_retain_and_the_members_equity_position` clause 1 —
  "Where the member's equity balance stands at or above the maximum the class the equity account is
  held under allows, nothing is retained" — is the source's `overwrite.replaced_by` verbatim, while
  the source's `compute` guards it with `equity_ceiling > 0`. On a class whose posted ceiling is
  0.00 the two diverge completely. No effect here (Class A Voting Membership, ceiling 500,000.00).
  Source-side.
- **P5 — a term used with two extensions inside one YAML.** "applied to the contract" is bound to
  `disposition='contract_application'` in `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation.compute` and to
  every `grain_delivery_applied` row in `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge.compute` and
  `grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge.compute`. This is the source half of F1/F2 and is the deeper
  of the two causes.
- **P6 — catalogue charges no write books.** The programme catalogue makes the setup fee at
  countersigning, the amendment fee and the per-bushel extension charge normative, and no task tool
  in this difficulty takes a parameter that books any of them. The documents carry the source
  faithfully; recorded so it is on the record.

## dependency_form

Basis: the blind answer's hop marks for this task (all three hops **state-derived**, none
pre-solved) and a full read of the 73-document corpus.

### F3 — `KB-EXPLICIT RED`: the baseline computation document tells the reader a variation exists

**Document:** `docs/grain/striking_the_balance_still_owed_512f95c7.json` (role `baseline`), "How the
credit is assembled".

**Quotation, the two sentences in sequence:**

> "No handling shrink is taken on conditioned loads. Handling shrink on conditioned loads, **where it
> arises at all**, is taken on the net bushels of every load standing against the contract, whatever
> the facility and whatever the disposition, meaning the loads applied to the contract and the loads
> run straight through together."

**What it states.** The first sentence is the factor's baseline value and belongs there. The second
states, of a quantity just declared nil, the base it is taken on — and hedges that statement with
"where it arises at all". Stating the base of a quantity that is always nil has no purpose, and the
hedge says as much: read together, the two sentences tell the reader that this nil is conditional and
that something elsewhere can lift it. The corpus is meant to be a discrete topology in which the
existence of a factor is discovered from the customer's records alone — here it is discovered from
the computation document. The other six baseline documents in this product carry their nil defaults
flat ("The repeat surcharge is nil", "The patron release factor is one", "No collection charge is
added", "the freight differential recovered is nil…") and hedge nothing; this one is the exception.

A second consequence, recorded for completeness: because the base of the conditioned handling shrink
lives in the baseline document, the factor document
`handling_shrink_on_conditioned_loads_0b04605a.json` states only that the shrink is "taken on the
loads standing against a contract" and never pins the base in the source's terms.

### Observations that fall short of RED, recorded so the judgement can be rechecked

- **`loss_multiplier_and_what_was_delivered_2c7424ef.json`**, illustration: "9,000 undelivered
  bushels **at a release rate of 0.16** come to 1,080.00 before the patron release factor." 0.16 is
  the *delivered release rate*, a tier value of the `release_rate_basis` factor carried in another
  document, and it matches no programme's default penalty (0.00 / 0.15 / 0.15 / 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.25 /
  0.30), which is what the buyout baseline gives as the release rate. A reader who cross-checks could
  infer from it that some other release rate exists. I stop short of RED because the sentence is
  framed as a hypothetical figure, states no condition under which 0.16 applies, and the
  release-rate ladder is in any case discoverable from the contract's programme; but the figure would
  be better drawn from outside another factor's ladder.
- **"before the patron release factor", "before the multiplier and the factor", "before the
  hauled-load credit and the forward reserve"** in `loss_multiplier_and_what_was_delivered`,
  `release_rate_kept_on_bushels_released` and `share_of_production_allowed_to_stand_sold`: each names
  a quantity that the corresponding **baseline** document already names in its assembly ("The patron
  release factor is one", "No hauled-load credit is added. The forward reserve is the standard
  forward reserve of 3000 bushels"). Naming an assembly slot is not disclosing a variation, so these
  are not findings.
- **`which_charges_a_statement_draws_6bf13373.json`**: "because the desk clears the ledger each time
  it pays a live contract out" is an added rationale, not an added norm, and states no dependency.

### Checks that came back clean

- **No state-form sentence restated as an action.** All five prerequisite sentences in this product
  are `form: state`, each appears verbatim exactly once in the whole scenario, in a document of the
  problem it blocks, and neither hub restates it in action terms. `releasing_a_members_grain_money`
  never says "book the carry first" or "put the roll through first"; it says only what the money
  waits on. `putting_a_futures_month_roll_through` never says "restate the balance"; it says only
  what the charge waits on.
- **No other problem's tool name, anywhere.** Each of the seven recorded acts is named in exactly one
  document — its own hub's "How it is invoked" block.
- **No route, no aggregated chain, no ordered step list across problems.** No document carries a
  dependency table, a checklist, a roadmap or a procedure spanning two problems. The only ordering
  sentences in the corpus outside the prerequisite sentences are base-law clauses the source itself
  states ("A signed roll instruction … is registered with the grain desk before the roll is
  executed", "A signed master grain marketing agreement … is on file for the member before the
  contract is opened"), which the KB may neither drop nor soften; these are recorded as policy-side
  notes, not as KB findings.
- **No contrast of a wrong with a correct reading, no named mistake, no cross-problem worked example
  or FAQ.** The "Points of judgement" sections stay inside one policy each.
- **Titles and openings.** All seven hub titles and all seven baseline titles name general subjects
  ("Releasing a Member's Money on a Settlement Statement", "Restating the Bushels Still Owed on a
  Grain Marketing Contract", "What the Delayed Price Carry Comes To"). None restates a customer
  request or labels a procedure for a specific situation. Openings likewise.
- **Findability of depended-on documents in the records' own words.** "delayed price service charge",
  "roll confirmation" and "bushels still owed" are the words the prerequisite sentences use and the
  words the depended-on documents use; none of the three hops needed phrasing borrowed from the
  dependent document.
- **No factor document says which tier a customer falls on.** Search for "this member", "the caller",
  "most members", "in this case" returns nothing; every illustration is labelled hypothetical.

**`KB-EXPLICIT RED`** on F3.

thirteen catalogue tables and the four tool contracts — corresponds losslessly at the level of
entailment. Nothing that passed in revision 1 has regressed, and the re-render added no claim from
outside the source.
